title: Cabling and Physical Interface Issues

header.html: 5.2 Given a scenario, troubleshoot common cabling and physical interface issues: cable issues (incorrect cable, signal degradation, improper termination, TX/RX transposed); interface issues (increasing interface counters: CRC, runts, giants, drops; port status: error disabled, administratively down, suspended); hardware issues (PoE budget exceeded, incorrect standard; transceiver mismatch and signal strength)
the official CompTIA Network+ N10-009 exam objectives, version 4.0

html:
1Cable issues

Problem Symptoms and cause
Incorrect cable Wrong type: single-mode vs multimode fiber mismatch, wrong Cat rating (Cat 5 for 10 Gbps), STP vs UTP in a noisy area, crossover vs straight-through
Signal degradation Crosstalk (signal bleeds between pairs), interference (EMI from motors, lights, power cables), attenuation (signal weakens over distance: cable too long)
Improper termination Bad punch-down or crimp, wrong pinout (568A vs 568B), untwisted pairs near the connector: slow or intermittent links, errors
TX/RX transposed Fiber transmit and receive swapped: no link light; flip the fiber pair

Exam tip

. Cat 5e/6 copper runs are limited to 100 meters. Link lights off on fiber = check TX/RX and the transceiver.

2Interface issues

Counter Meaning
CRC errors Frames failed the cyclic redundancy check: bad cable, interference, duplex mismatch, bad NIC
Runts Frames smaller than the minimum 64 bytes: collisions or a duplex mismatch
Giants Frames larger than the maximum (over 1518 bytes unless jumbo is on): MTU mismatch or a faulty NIC
Drops Frames discarded, often from congestion or full buffers
Port status Meaning
Error disabled The switch shut the port down because of a violation (port security, BPDU guard, link flaps); fix the cause, then re-enable
Administratively down Someone ran "shutdown"; run "no shutdown"
Suspended A link aggregation port that did not match the bundle (settings, LACP)
Exam tip

. Rising CRC errors point to the cable or interference. "Err-disabled" means a security feature fired. "Administratively down" means someone disabled it.

3Hardware issues

Problem Meaning
PoE budget exceeded The switch cannot power all devices (total wattage too high); some PoE devices lose power; move devices, use a bigger power budget or a different switch
Incorrect PoE standard A device needs more power than the port offers (802.3af 15.4 W, 802.3at 30 W, 802.3bt 60 to 90 W)
Transceiver mismatch Different speed, wavelength, fiber type or protocol at the two ends: no link
Signal strength Optical power too low or too high: dirty connector, bad fiber, wrong optic; check with a power meter
Exam tip

. CRC errors point to the cable; err-disabled means a security feature shut the port; administratively down means someone shut it.

4Exam Q&A

4.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1A switch port shows a rapidly increasing CRC error count. What is the most likely cause?

  • AA VLAN misconfiguration
  • BA faulty cable or electromagnetic interference
  • CA missing default gateway
  • DAn expired DHCP lease
Show the answer

Answer: B. CRC errors point to physical-layer problems.

S2A fiber link shows no light after installation, although both transceivers are the same type. What should be checked first?

  • AThe DNS server address
  • BThe spanning tree root bridge
  • CThe DHCP scope
  • DWhether the transmit and receive fibers are swapped
Show the answer

Answer: D. Transposed TX and RX fibers cause no link.

S3A switch port is shown as err-disabled after a security violation. What should the technician do?

  • AReplace the cable immediately
  • BFix the cause, then re-enable the port
  • CChange the VLAN of every port
  • DIncrease the MTU
Show the answer

Answer: B. Err-disabled ports need the cause fixed before re-enabling.

S4Several IP cameras lose power when a new camera is added to a PoE switch. What is the likely cause?

  • AA duplex mismatch
  • BA native VLAN mismatch
  • CThe PoE power budget is exceeded
  • DExcessive TTL
Show the answer

Answer: C. The switch's total PoE budget cannot supply all devices.

S5A 10 Gbps link over Cat 5 cable runs at 100 Mbps with errors. What is the best fix?

  • AReduce the MTU
  • BEnable port mirroring
  • CReplace it with the correct higher-category cable
  • DAdd a DHCP relay
Show the answer

Answer: C. The cable category does not support the speed.

S6Which port status means an administrator shut the port down?

  • AError disabled
  • BSuspended
  • CForwarding
  • DAdministratively down
Show the answer

Answer: D. The shutdown command sets administratively down.

4.2 Recall questions

R1What does a CRC error indicate?

Show the answer

A corrupted frame, usually from a physical-layer problem.

R2What is a runt?

Show the answer

A frame smaller than the minimum size.

R3What is a giant?

Show the answer

A frame larger than the maximum size.

R4What is attenuation?

Show the answer

Signal weakening over distance.

R5What does "suspended" mean on a port?

Show the answer

A bundled port that does not match the link aggregation settings.

R6What is the maximum length of a copper Ethernet run?

Show the answer

100 meters.

5Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Cable wrong type, crosstalk, EMI, attenuation, bad termination, TX/RX swapped, 100 m limit
Counters CRC (cable or interference), runts (collisions, duplex), giants (MTU), drops (congestion)
Status err-disabled (violation), administratively down (shutdown), suspended (LACP mismatch)
Hardware PoE budget, PoE standard, transceiver mismatch, optical signal strength
